transcript.text: gas hob keeps clickin on its own since i cleand it, stops then starts agen. drivin me mad. pls help

First switch it off at the wall or cooker switch and let it cool completely. That clicking sound is the ignition system trying to light a burner that isn't detecting a flame. Since this started after cleaning, it is most likely that water or cleaning fluid has seeped under a burner cap or onto the electrode (the small white ceramic tip near the gas hole), causing it to spark continuously. Please turn off the gas supply for safety. Lift off each burner cap and base plate you can remove. Check if they are completely dry and seated perfectly flat. If any look wet, dirty, or slightly out of place, clean them with a cloth, ensure they are bone dry, and reseat them firmly so they sit level. Let me know what you find.
ok i took the caps off when cleaning and sloshed loads of water about. one cap looked a bit wonky so i put it back proper. no gas smell tho

Since you sloshed water around, moisture is almost certainly causing the ignition system to spark continuously or fail to detect a flame. Even a tiny amount of water on the electrode can cause this 'phantom' clicking. Please switch off the gas supply again for safety. Take all burner caps and bases off one by one. Wipe them completely dry, including the area underneath where they sit on the hob surface. Also gently wipe the small white ceramic tip (the spark electrode) near each burner base to remove any cleaning residue or water. Reassemble everything carefully, making sure every cap sits perfectly flat and level—this is crucial for flame detection. Once you are sure it is dry and seated correctly, turn the gas back on and try lighting a burner normally. Let me know if the clicking stops.

ok i wiped the grease off round the igniter and put the wonky cap back flat. i also unplugged the hob at the plug under the sink for the afternoon and the clicking has stopped. is it ok to plug it back in?

[Heading: Moisture on ignition electrode causing phantom sparking]
Yes, it is safe to plug the hob back in now that the clicking has stopped. The issue was almost certainly residual moisture on the spark electrode from the cleaning water you sloshed around; drying it out and letting the electronics reset (by unplugging) cleared the fault. Before you start cooking again, please double-check that all burner caps are sitting perfectly flat and level—this is crucial for proper flame detection. If the clicking returns while you are using the hob, switch it off immediately at the plug and call an engineer, as this could indicate a deeper electrical issue or a wet thermocouple. Otherwise, you should be good to go.
